findings.title: Migration crashes when no category matches embed_category
findings.body: The lookup `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` calls `[]` on the result and then `['id']` on the row. `embed_category` defaults to '' and most installs never set it, so no row matches, `[0]` is nil, and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same pattern on line 15 (`[0]['value']` for uncategorized_category_id) has the same problem. Upgrades on typical sites would fail. The lookup should handle an empty result set, falling back to uncategorized.

findings.title: Host values interpolated into SQL without escaping
findings.body: Each host from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is spliced directly into an INSERT string. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and aborts the migration. Use parameterized inserts or quote the value with the connection's quoting helper.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If the request omits `host` (or sends null), `self.host` is nil and the save raises NoMethodError, which becomes a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard for blank host before the substitutions.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the URI side
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column. The `host` taken from `URI(...)` is passed through unchanged, so a referer or embed_url with uppercase letters (e.g. `EvilTrout.com`) never matches a stored host. The input should be downcased before comparison, which also means `host_allowed?` can reject valid embeds.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, either in validations or in a unique index. `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so duplicates silently pick an arbitrary category for TopicEmbed imports. Add a uniqueness validation (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index.

findings.title: update and destroy crash with 500 for unknown ids
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing record, and `save_host(nil)` or `host.destroy` then raises NoMethodError. This should return 404 (for example via `find` / `find_by!`).

findings.title: update action is a no-op that reports success
findings.body: `update` never reads params or persists anything; it just re-renders the unchanged embedding. The client's `saveChanges` calls it with `{}`, so the admin UI looks saved when nothing was. Either implement the update or remove the route and the save action.

findings.title: has_many with embed: :ids sends only ids, not the hosts
findings.body: With `embed: :ids` and no include, the payload contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no `embeddable_hosts` collection. The client's `_hydrateEmbedded` then looks up each id in a root collection that doesn't exist and produces an array of undefined entries, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` renders broken rows. The hosts need to be side-loaded (include) or the client must fetch them.

findings.title: Unresolved _ids entries stored as undefined
findings.body: In the `_ids` branch, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for any id not present in the root payload, and `map` keeps those as undefined entries. Those entries are then assigned to the model's collection. Missing ids should be filtered out, and the `|| []` fallback is dead code because `map` always returns an array.

findings.title: Fabricator files have swapped contents
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now holds only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the :category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. This is misleading to maintainers. The category fabricators should be in category_fabricator.rb and the embeddable host fabricator in its own file.
